newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Prosecutors question S.Korean Kim's son over Hanbo.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors question S.Korean Kim's son over Hanbo.

text.p: South Korean prosecutors said on Friday they were questioning a son of President Kim Young-sam in connection with massive loans to the failed Hanbo Steel Co.
Kim Hyun-chul, the president's second son, filed a libel complaint on Tuesday against six opposition politicians who accused him of peddling influence in giving the loans.

President Kim's political credibility has already been badly damaged by a loans-for-kickback scandal involving Hanbo. Three of Kim's close associates were arrested on charges of bribery in connection with the case.
Kim Hyun-chul has said he had nothing to do with five trillion won ($5.8 billion) of loans that Hanbo Steel racked up before being declared insolvent on January 23.
Senior prosecutor Choi Byung-koog told reporters that the prosecution would first focus on the libel complaint but also investigate suspicions raised by opposition members.
The opposition has criticised state prosecutors for what it sees as a failure to reveal the truth behind the scandal. It has called for a fresh prosecution probe.
